doc.title: Bob Magnusson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Building repertoire through after-hours gigs and jam sessions
summary: He was learning tunes, playing after-hours and at Joe and Tony Morello's house, and calls it lifelong learning.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Wow. You had said previously that you didn’t know any tunes, like when you went with Buddy.
Had you worked up your repertoire some?
By the time I worked with Sarah?

Yeah I was starting. I mean I’ve never been what I call a tunesmith, but I was trying to learn tunes and build up repertoire. And like playing that jazz gig after hours. And if I didn’t have a jazz gig I would be out at a guy’s house, some guys, Joe Morello, he’s also

an Upstate, from Niagara Falls, he and Tony Morello. They were friends I had there. We would play any hour. Sometimes it was just him and I, tenor sax and bass we would play. Well here’s how this tune goes. Because it’s such a learning — I mean still at this point I’m still learning stuff. It’s a lifelong learning venture, as you know being a musician yourself. So I was trying to build some repertoire and learn some things.
